exemptions.title: Ensure Authentication Required for Single User Mode
exemptions.why: AWS Marketplace policy prohibits meeting this rule in an AMI: "AMI must not contain hardcoded secrets such as system user and service passwords (including hashed passwords)" and "Password-based authentication for instance services is prohibited. This applies even if the password is generated, reset, or defined by the user at launch"; Linux AMIs "must allow users to get fully privileged access (for example, to allow sudo access)" (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/marketplace/latest/userguide/product-and-ami-policies.html). The rule needs a boot loader or root password hash in the image, or a sudo password for the key-only default user.
exemptions.customer_action: After launch run `sudo stigready-set-credentials` (installed in the image): it sets your own GRUB superuser and password, root password and a sudo password for your admin user, and removes NOPASSWD, which meets this rule on your instance.

exemptions.title: Ensure Red Hat GPG Key Installed
exemptions.why: The check passes only when the OS is RHEL and Red Hat's own signing keys are installed (gpg-pubkey-fd431d51, the Red Hat release key, plus that release's auxiliary key).
